newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Robust demand powers tight oil market - IEA.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Robust demand powers tight oil market - IEA.

text.p: World oil supplies have risen far more slowly than expected this year, helping underpin oil prices in a market led by robust demand growth among the world's industrialised powers, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.

"Oil markets were much tighter than expected in June and July as the absence of Iraqi exports was compounded by supply shortfalls from several areas and strong demand" the agency said in its monthly Oil Market Report.
Analysts said the IEA report underscored the oil market's resilience following a two-month delay in the resumption of Iraqi exports under the United Nations' oil-for-food exchange.
"It tells us that demand, especially in the U.S. has been strong and that supplies, not for the first time, have not met expectations," said a London-based oil analyst.
Benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude was trading at $18.77 a barrel on Friday after touching a low for the year at $17.30 in early June.
Iraqi oil is expected to start flowing again next week but IEA figures show lean crude inventories in the West leave plenty of space to soak up at least initial liftings.

Commercial oil stocks held in Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries rose by just 480,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the second quarter of the year, the smallest second quarter increase since the 1991 Gulf War, the IEA said.
The agency made hefty downward revisions to its non-OPEC supply forecast cutting an average of almost 500,000 barrels a day (bpd) from previous estimates through to the end of 1998.

The Paris-based IEA said its reduced projections for non-OPEC supply reflected "the recent underperformance in the North Sea and Australia," and downward revisions to data for some developing countries.
Oil analysts have in the past criticised the IEA for painting a skewed picture of world oil supply-demand fundamentals by giving to much weight to expected non-OPEC crude flows.

IEA forecasts for strong growth in world demand this year were left unchanged at 73.8 million bpd, a rise of 1.9 million bpd or 2.6 percent on last year. It expects a similar climb in demand to 75.7 million next year.
The agency said strong second quarter demand, up 3.9 percent, "was led by robust U.S. and firm German demand growth in June complementing ongoing demand growth in Asia and Latin America."
It said it had reassessed North American demand growth for 1998 in the light of strong increases so far this year.
The IEA's latest forecasts make happier reading than of late for OPEC which the agency now says has more room to manoeuvre on the supply front for the remainder of the year.
